Company: Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Ltd
BusinessModel: The company runs mutual funds and sells investment advice. It earns a fee on every rupee customers park in its schemes. Canara Bank owns 51% and Robeco (Netherlands) owns 49%, making it India's 2nd-oldest AMC (1993).
RevenueStreams: Mutual fund management fees - dominant (FY25); investment advisory fees (FY25); equity vs debt scheme split: data not found
Expenses: Employee and fund operating costs: data not found; asset-light model with OPM 65% (FY25)
TAM: India mutual fund AUM ~Rs 70 lakh crore (2025, AMFI); SIP flows ~Rs 27,000 crore/month (2025)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Management fees on AUM growth; SIP/retail inflows via Canara Bank network; operating leverage on fixed cost base

BusinessModel: The company builds and runs solar and wind power plants across India. It sells electricity under long-term contracts, mostly to government-linked buyers. Parent NTPC owns it; largest renewable PSU in India excluding hydro (Sep 2024).
RevenueStreams: Solar power sales under PPAs - majority of capacity (FY25); wind power sales under PPAs (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Interest Rs 694 crore (FY24) rising to ~Rs 898 crore (FY26E); depreciation Rs 643 crore (FY24) rising to ~Rs 1,102 crore (FY26E)
TAM: India targets ~500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030; NTPC group targets ~60 GW renewables by 2032
PL_Top3_Contributors: New capacity commissioning adds contracted revenue; depreciation and interest burden from capex; PPA tariffs and curtailment risk on solar

BusinessModel: The company makes and sells cars in India - 13 models across hatchbacks, sedans, SUVs and EVs, plus parts and service. Korea's Hyundai Motor Group owns it; India's 2nd-largest vehicle exporter (Apr 2021-Jun 2024).
RevenueStreams: SUVs - dominant share of volumes (FY25); hatchbacks/entry cars (FY25); exports, spares and service (FY25); mix %: data not found
Expenses: Raw materials/components - dominant cost, %: data not found; total expenses ~Rs 62,760 crore TTM; borrowings only ~Rs 1,098 crore
TAM: India passenger vehicle market ~4.3 million units/year (FY24-FY25, SIAM); SUVs over half of domestic sales
PL_Top3_Contributors: SUV mix and pricing; commodity and freight costs vs 12-13% OPM; volume leverage across plants

Company: Anand Rathi Share & Stock Brokers Ltd
BusinessModel: The company runs a full-service stock brokerage. It earns broking commissions, lends money to clients for trading, and distributes mutual funds and investment products to retail, HNI and institutional clients.
RevenueStreams: Broking and margin trading facilities - core (FY25); distribution of investment products (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Interest/financing cost on margin book Rs 147 crore (FY25); depreciation Rs 25 crore (FY25); employee costs: data not found
TAM: India ~19 crore demat accounts (FY25, CDSL/NSDL); broking revenue pool in tens of thousands of crore rupees annually
PL_Top3_Contributors: Cash/F&O broking volumes; margin-trading interest spread; distribution income from mutual funds

BusinessModel: The company owns and runs luxury hotels - seven properties with 1,836 keys including 245 serviced apartments - across Indian cities, all under the Hyatt brand. Largest owner of Hyatt-affiliated hotels in India.
RevenueStreams: Room revenue from luxury hotels - majority (FY25); food & beverage/banquets (FY25); serviced apartments and other income (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Interest Rs 88 crore (FY26); depreciation Rs 91 crore (FY26); total expenses Rs 528 crore (FY26); staff/energy: data not found
TAM: Indian hotel industry revenue in tens of billions of US$ (IBEF 2024); premium supply lags demand in key cities
PL_Top3_Contributors: Occupancy and room-rate gains across Hyatt portfolio; banquets/F&B weddings business; operating leverage over fixed interest and depreciation

BusinessModel: The company makes sponge iron, steel billets and TMT bars under the 'Vraj' brand at plants in Chhattisgarh, selling mainly to construction buyers. Gopal Sponge and Power holds a controlling stake.
RevenueStreams: TMT bars - main construction product (FY25); sponge iron and MS billets, partly captive (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Raw materials iron ore and coal dominate, %: data not found; total expenses Rs 412 crore (FY25); depreciation Rs 8 crore; interest Rs 2-3 crore (FY25)
TAM: India steel consumption ~145-150 million tonnes (FY24-FY25, worldsteel)
PL_Top3_Contributors: TMT price vs iron ore/coal spread; volume growth from Raipur expansion (TTM sales +29%); captive power integration margin

BusinessModel: The company lends money for homes - mortgages, loans against property, developer finance and lease-rental loans. Bajaj Finance owns it fully; 2nd-largest HFC in India with AUM Rs 1,33,412 crore (Dec 2025).
RevenueStreams: Home mortgages and commercial-property loans - core (FY25); LAP and lease-rental discounting (FY25); developer finance (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Interest on borrowings - dominant cost on Rs 82,072 crore book (FY25); opex Rs 759 crore (FY25); provisions: data not found
TAM: India housing credit ~Rs 33-35 lakh crore outstanding (FY24-FY25, RBI/NHB); mortgage penetration ~11-12% of GDP
PL_Top3_Contributors: Loan book growth ~25-30% at stable spreads; cost of funds vs lending yield; credit costs/NPA performance

BusinessModel: The company makes stainless-steel seamless and welded pipes and tubes at Mehsana, Gujarat, serving oil and gas, chemicals, fertilizers, power, pharma, automotive and railways. Listed via IPO in 2025.
RevenueStreams: SS seamless pipes and instrumentation tubes - main source (FY26); SS seamless tubes and U-tubes (FY26); SS welded tubes/U-tubes - expansion in progress (FY26); split %: data not found
Expenses: Stainless steel/nickel raw materials - dominant, %: data not found; interest Rs 26 crore (FY26 TTM); total expenses Rs 468 crore TTM
TAM: India SS tube/pipe market in low tens of thousands of crore rupees annually (industry estimates, early 2020s)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Nickel/SS raw-material price spread; seamless volumes to oil/gas/pharma/chemicals; new welded-tube capacity scale-up

BusinessModel: The company sells jewellery through its own 'Vaibhav Jewellers' retail chain across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, focused on affordable daily-wear and wedding gold jewellery. Listed via IPO in 2023.
RevenueStreams: Gold jewellery - dominant share (FY25); studded/diamond jewellery and silver - smaller (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Cost of gold/raw materials ~80%+ of sales, exact %: data not found; interest Rs 41 crore (FY25); total expenses Rs 2,217 crore (FY25)
TAM: India jewellery market ~US$ 80-100 billion annually (FY24-FY25, IBEF/industry)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Gold price and volume; new showroom additions in AP/Telangana; studded-jewellery mix lift

BusinessModel: The company builds and installs equipment that keeps telecom towers and solar plants running - DC power systems, lithium batteries, monitoring systems and inverters - with turnkey installation and commissioning. NSE SME IPO in 2025.
RevenueStreams: Telecom infrastructure - DC power systems and turnkey installation, dominant (FY24-FY25); lithium batteries and energy storage (FY25); solar inverters (FY25); split %: data not found
Expenses: Raw materials - electronics and lithium cells - dominant, %: data not found; expenses Rs 1,876 crore (FY25) vs Rs 1,995 crore (FY24)
TAM: India telecom capex ~US$ 10-12 billion annually during 5G rollout (FY23-FY25, industry estimates); storage and inverter markets growing 20%+
PL_Top3_Contributors: Large telecom-infrastructure order wins; lithium cell and power-electronics input costs; receivables/working capital from PSU-style customers
